query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Categorical theme extracted from review text with well-separated, human-readable levels (poor_rude, warm_proactive, professional_adequate, inconsistent) that are near-balanced. Ideal for segmenting Overall Rating and cross-tabbing with Type of Traveller/Class.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Interpretable four-level theme (consistent_low, consistent_high, inconsistent_by_leg, inconsistent_by_crew) with healthy support in every bucket; supports meaningful comparison of ratings across consistency patterns.

per_column.name: service_frequency_complaint
per_column.rationale: Clean boolean flag with a clear semantic meaning. It is skewed (~5.7% true), so the comparison rests on a smaller subgroup, but 460 rows is still enough to contrast mean rating between the two groups.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: Thematic decomposition of comfort remarks (adequate, comfortable_spacious, cramped_narrow, broken_defective) with interpretable categories. High NULL share (~38%, theme not mentioned) shrinks the compared population but is itself an informative 'mentioned vs not' contrast. Distinct from the existing numeric Seat Comfort rating, not a restatement of the focus.

per_column.name: food_quality_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordinal-like sentiment (positive/adequate/negative) over food. High NULL (~45%) reduces coverage but the non-null levels remain well separated and comparable against Overall Rating.

per_column.name: special_meal_handling
per_column.rationale: Interpretable niche boolean. Heavily skewed (~4.3% true), so it is close to near-constant and offers only weak comparative power, but the true group (345) is still a legitimate segment for a targeted comparison.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: Well-separated categories (poorly_handled_dismissive, proactive_excellent, adequate) with an explicit not_applicable gate. The applicable subset (~2600) yields a strong, interpretable relationship to rating; not_applicable is a coherent segment rather than opaque noise.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Interpretable multi-level theme (poor_rude, smooth_positive, disorganized_slow, adequate) covering a review dimension not in the original numeric columns; supports clear segmentation despite a ~42% NULL share.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Balanced, human-readable levels (responsive_helpful, unresponsive_rude, not_contacted, slow_inadequate) with strong support in each; an excellent associational variable for comparing Overall Rating.

per_column.name: value_for_class_perception
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, well-populated expectation scale (poor_value → exceeds_expectations) that ties value to the booked Class, directly enabling the requested Class-conditioned analysis of rating. Distinct theme, not a restatement of Overall Rating.

per_column.name: class_product_expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordinal gap (below_expectation/met/exceeded) with strong support in all levels; a natural segmentation for how the class product relates to Overall Rating across traveller types.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: Interpretable boolean capturing a 'things got worse' narrative. Skewed (~7.6% true) so comparative power is modest, but 619 rows form a usable segment for contrasting rating.

judge.rationale: The set is a strong fit for exploratory analysis: nearly every column is an external, associational theme mined from the free-text Reviews field and expressed as named, well-separated categories or clean booleans rather than opaque scores, so a human can group/segment on them and compare Overall Rating across Type of Traveller and Class. None restate the focus (Overall Rating), and even columns overlapping existing numeric ratings (seat_comfort_issue, food_quality_sentiment, value_for_class_perception) add interpretable categorical framing. Deductions: (1) three boolean flags (service_frequency_complaint ~5.7%, special_meal_handling ~4.3%, service_decline_perception ~7.6%) are heavily skewed toward near-constant, limiting comparative leverage; (2) several themes carry large NULL/not_applicable shares (~38–67%), which shrink the compared subpopulations even though the 'mentioned vs not' split is itself informative. Overall, the columns realise the EDA claim well, hence a high but not perfect informativeness score.
